subject: OEM & Cloud capacity sync — GPU procurement lead times and delivery options

From: Kevin Zhou <kevin.zhou@superchip.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial OEM quote and lead times for SuperChip SUP-1000 series

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the conversation earlier — attaching our preliminary quote for the SUP-1000 GPU assemblies (SUP-1000-40U rack nodes) and standard support terms (file: SUPER-1000_OEM_quote_v1.pdf). Key items: 

- Lead time: estimated 12–16 weeks from PO for custom-configured nodes.
- Quick-ship option: we have a limited pool of pre-configured nodes that can ship in ~6 weeks (smaller quantity, premium applies).
- Minimum order: 8 nodes for direct ship; tiered pricing at 8/24/48 units.
- Partial shipments: possible with 30% deposit, balance on delivery.
- Warranty/Advance replacement: 12 months with optional on-site SLA (upgradeable).

We understand you may be pairing this with Reserved Cloud capacity as a bridge. If you can share (a) expected go-live window, (b) target concurrency (QPS / typical seq length), and (c) whether you can accept staged delivery, we can firm up lead-time commitments and whether we can allocate a faster production lane.

Cc'd Alicia from AusCloud in case a hybrid plan is needed.

Best,
Kevin

Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial OEM quote and lead times for SuperChip SUP-1000 series

Kevin — thanks for the quick turnaround and the quote. A few points and asks from our side so we can map to the deal timeline (RDW-4567):

1) Deal timing: customer NovaRetail expects pilot capacity by 2026-06-15 and production by 2026-08-01. We need a clear mutual action plan to hit pilot date.
2) Sizing: target initial Dedicated footprint = 24 SUP-1000 nodes (we may expand to 48 in Q4). Typical seq length ~1024 tokens; peak concurrent sessions approx 120 (with batching).
3) Hybrid fallback: we intend to reserve cloud capacity in us-west-2 as a fallback during ramp; Alicia, can you confirm reservation lead times and burst guarantees?
4) Procurement asks: can you provide 1) an explicit per-node lead-time commit for the 24 quantity, 2) expedited lane cost (if available), and 3) examples of staggered delivery schedules you have executed recently?
5) Contracting: we prefer 30% deposit + balance on delivery terms but need finance/PO language for review.

Monica — can you open a procurement ticket and start the Contract Review / PO cadence once Kevin confirms the formal commercial terms?

Short next steps: Kevin to confirm firm lead-time and staging options; Alicia to confirm cloud reservation timing; Monica to prep PO template.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@auscloud.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity & burst options for us-west-2 (response to lead-time sync)

Hi Karthik —

Quick note on cloud capacity in us-west-2: 

- Reserved pool build: we can carve a Reserved GPU pool within 3–4 weeks after signed commitment for standard VM families (subject to regional availability).
- Guaranteed capacity: for specialized accelerators we advise commitment 6+ weeks ahead; for broadly-available instances we can usually do 3–4 weeks.
- Burst/fallback: short-term burst to on-demand possible for up to 20% beyond reserved baseline; beyond that runs at regular on-demand market rates and may be throttled if region is constrained.
- Contracting path: we can provision a reservation commitment and a short-term capacity hold while your PO is processed (requires 10% non-refundable reservation fee).

Actionable link: https://partner.auscloud.com/reservations/rdw-4567 (internal capacity reservation portal)
HubSpot ref: 8910

If you plan to stagger OEM deliveries, we recommend reserving at least the pilot capacity (8–12 nodes) immediately to avoid a mid-May shortage we are already seeing in us-west-2.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Enterprise Cloud Sales — AusCloud
alicia.gomez@auscloud.com

Attachment: CloudCapacity_SLA_us-west-2.xlsx

Subject: FW: OEM & Cloud capacity sync — next steps for procurement and finance

Monica / Rishi — forwarding the vendor/cloud replies. Summary and asks: 

Summary:
- SuperChip (Kevin) is quoting 12–16 week standard lead times; limited quick-ship inventory at ~6 weeks for a premium.
- AusCloud (Alicia) can reserve baseline cloud capacity in ~3–4 weeks, but recommends committing pilot capacity now to avoid mid-May shortages.

Asks (procurement / finance):
1) Monica — please open a formal procurement ticket and request SuperChip SOW + final commercial quote. Start negotiation on deposit terms (target: 30% deposit; ask them to accept escrow schedule if needed).
2) Rishi — please confirm whether Finance will approve a 30% deposit for staggered delivery and whether net-30 terms are required on the balance. Also flag any cross-border payment constraints if SuperChip invoices from their EMEA subsidiary.
3) Marissa — please align the customer (NovaRetail) on a staged pilot acceptance plan (8–12 nodes in pilot, remaining nodes for prod) and confirm whether the customer accepts partial-delivery milestones.

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
- 4/09: SuperChip to provide firm per-node lead-time and staging options (requested).
- 4/12: Redwood to finalize procurement terms and send PO template to SuperChip.
- 4/15: AusCloud to provision pilot reservation upon receiving reservation fee/commitment.
- 6/15: Pilot go-live (target)

Lower-risk option: If SuperChip cannot guarantee 6–8 week availability for pilot units we should lock equivalent capacity via AusCloud for the pilot window and accept staged OEM delivery for production.

Thanks — let me know if you need me to open the PO draft or join any negotiation calls.

Karthik

Subject: Re: OEM & Cloud capacity sync — updated lead times and partial-ship proposal

Karthik and team — apologies for the delay; pulled internal production planning. Answers below and updated commercial approach: 

1) Firm lead times for 24-node order: we can commit to a staged delivery model — 12 nodes in 7–8 weeks, remaining 12 nodes in an additional 6–8 weeks (total 13–16 weeks for the full order). This assumes approval of the 30% deposit and a signed SOW within 5 business days.

2) Expedited lane: we can allocate limited quick-ship inventory for up to 8 nodes at a premium of +12% per-node; lead time ~5–6 weeks for that tranche.

3) Staggered delivery logistics: we will perform factory acceptance testing on each tranche and provide a manifest + ASN for each shipment. We can coordinate with your on-site team for racking + acceptance; we also offer white-glove install (quote attached as an addendum).

4) Invoicing: SuperChip can accept 30% deposit, 60% on shipment of each tranche, 10% retention 30 days post-acceptance. We will invoice from our US entity to avoid cross-border complications.

5) Warranty & spare pool: we will include 2 hot-spare boards per tranche and an option to purchase an onsite spare kit — details in attached addendum.

DocuSign / SOW link: https://www.docusign.com/Envelope/ExampleId123

If you want to lock pilot capacity quickly, I recommend:
- Commit to a deposit for 8 pilot nodes (either quick-ship or first tranche) by 4/13 to hit the ~6–8 week window.

On Alicia's point — happy to coordinate staggered delivery with AusCloud reservations as a fallback for the pilot window.

Onwards — please confirm how you'd like the PO / deposit flow to proceed and Monica if you want a procurement call next week I can join.

Thanks,
Kevin
